claim: Pushover sends a message via POST to https://api.pushover.net/1/messages.json, authenticated with an application API token plus the recipient user/group key; messages support title, priority -2 to 2 (emergency), custom sound, supplementary url+url_title, image attachment up to 5MB, and HTML or monospace formatting, delivering to dedicated iOS, Android, and desktop browser push clients.
quote: send a POST request to https://api.pushover.net/1/messages.json with... token (your application's API token), user (your user/group key)... message ... html ... priority ... -2, -1, 0 (default), 1, 2 ... attachment ... url ... a supplementary URL

claim: Pushbullet pushes are created via POST to https://api.pushbullet.com/v2/pushes with an Access-Token header, supporting note, link, and file push types with title/body fields.
quote: POST https://api.pushbullet.com/v2/pushes ... Access-Token: <your_access_token_here> ... type ... note ... title ... body

claim: Pushbullet delivers pushes to Android, iOS, Chrome and Firefox browser extensions, and Windows desktop clients, with free accounts capped at 500 pushes per month.
quote: Pushbullet ... Android ... iOS ... Chrome ... Firefox ... Windows ... limited to 500 pushes per month

claim: Telegram Bot API calls use https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD_NAME; sendMessage takes a chat_id, supports parse_mode HTML and MarkdownV2 formatting plus inline-keyboard buttons via reply_markup, and delivers into a Telegram chat conversation (iOS, Android, desktop, web) rather than a dedicated push app.
quote: https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD_NAME ... Each bot is given a unique authentication token when it is created ... parse_mode ... MarkdownV2 ... HTML ... Inline keyboard attached to the message

claim: Slack incoming webhooks post a JSON payload (text or Block Kit blocks) to a unique webhook URL that is itself the credential and is bound to a single installer-chosen channel; they cannot upload files, delete posted messages, or override the channel, and deliver into a Slack channel (iOS, Android, desktop, web) rather than a dedicated push app.
quote: Creating an incoming webhook gives you a unique URL to which you send a JSON payload with the message text and some options ... you cannot override the default channel ... Incoming webhooks do not allow you to delete a message after it's been posted
